title: homophonic chromatic number (chi_b) -- does a non-bijective chart need fewer alphabets?
hypothesis: K4 is a homophonic chart cipher needing fewer than 3 decryption charts (chi_b < 3), which would also explain the frequency flattening
insights: Crib conflict chromatic numbers: chi_full (both conflict types, the published bound) = 3; chi_a (same-plaintext->diff-cipher only) = 3; chi_b (same-cipher->diff-plaintext only, the ONLY constraint on a homophonic decryption chart) = 2. Edge counts: a=12, b=10, both=22.

HOMOPHONIC LOOPHOLE OPEN: chi_b=2 < chi_full=3 -- a homophonic cipher (which is allowed the 12 'same-plaintext->different-cipher' conflicts as legitimate homophones) needs only 2 decryption charts, FEWER than the 3 proven for bijective alphabets. AND homophonic substitution flattens frequency (our Fact 2) by design. So K4 could be a 2-chart homophonic 'chart-based coding system' -- a model the bijective analysis (035/085/106) over-constrained.
